telemetry-bot: alert — route=/api/v1/chat stream token_tail_p99 spiked 2.3x in prod-west-1 at 2059876539. correlated with GPU SM imbalance and VRAM churn. dashboards: https://dash.redwood/prod-west-1/route-chat (auto-attach)

Maria G: saw the alert, opening perf dashboard now. :eyes:

Joel B: on it. quick check: are batch sizes changing per-route? could be a batcher heuristic flip from yesterday's rollout.

rahul: verified via logs: batcher changed to `batch_size_estimator=v2` at 2059870230 in prod-west-1 for canary. rollout 10% -> 100% over 4h.

Maria G: ok that aligns. profiler capture from one affected pod attached below.

SRE Sam: ```
# nvprof-like slice dump (snip)
GPU 0 slice-0 SM util: 12%  slice-1 SM util: 78%  slice-2 SM util: 81%  slice-3 SM util: 20%
VRAM alloc churn: +1.8GB/min
Kernel timeline: fused_attention_v3 -> small_matmul -> fused_attention_v3 -> large_conv
KV cache hit rate: 88% -> 63% during spike
Token tail latency p99: 1.2s -> 3.4s
```

Maria G: interesting — slice skew (slice-1/2 hot, others cold) + VRAM churn -> thrashing across slices. looks like kernel-picker is producing varied allocations per request.

Joel B: is this the new kernel-picker change from the `kernel-selector` branch we pushed last week? it picks per-seqlen fused kernels which may allocate bigger workspace buffers.

rahul: yep that change went live with the estimator. combination of mixed seq_len traffic + continuous batching means different requests are being merged into batches that require different kernels.

ops-oncall: quick mitigation option: revert `batch_size_estimator=v2` to v1 on prod-west-1 canary group and throttle rollout.

Maria G: also add a short-term dashboard panel: "SM slice skew index" = (max_slice_util-min_slice_util)/mean_slice_util. set alert > 0.6. put per-route breakdown.

SRE Sam: suggestion to group by sequence length buckets in the batcher to reduce kernel heterogeneity. i.e., force batcher to assemble Hamming-homogeneous batches for 1s while backpressure warms up.

Joel B: patch ready: ```yaml
batcher:
  seqlen_grouping: true
  group_window_ms: 1000
  max_grouped_batch: 64
kernel-selector:
  prefer_fused: false # conservative
```

rahul: deploying the conservative kernel-selector flag to 100% of prod-west-1 now. will monitor.

telemetry-bot: deploy-bot reports: rollout of `kernel-selector.prefer_fused=false` completed at 2059876572 on prod-west-1-canary, 100%.

telemetry-bot: metric update (5m): token_tail_p99 for /api/v1/chat returned to 1.1x baseline, SM slice skew index dropped from 0.72 -> 0.28, VRAM churn reduced to +200MB/min.

Maria G: great. action items:
- rahul: tweak batcher config to prefer seqlen_grouping for mixed traffic (owner)
- Joel B: add the SM slice skew index panel and per-route P95/P99 token tail KPIs (owner)
- SRE Sam: add runbook steps for kernel-selector rollbacks and an alert runbook entry (owner)

rahul: starting on batcher change, will open PR with perf numbers from staging.

Joel B: I'll patch the dashboard. propose panels: per-route token_latency.{p50,p95,p99}, sm_slice_skew, vram_churn_rate, kernel_variant_ratio, kv_cache_hitrate. also a small table of top 10 routes by token_tail impact.

ops-oncall: adding a temporary suppression on alerts until the new dashboards are live (will expire in 6h). :hammer_and_wrench:

Maria G: long-term note: kernel-picker should expose estimated workspace size per kernel so batcher can avoid mixing incompatible kernels. file a design for kernel-selector <> batcher contract.

SRE Sam: logging note — add kernel_variant label to request traces so we can correlate per-request kernel choice with latency in tracing.

telemetry-bot: summary event created: https://issues.redwood/ID-4123 — "prod-west-1: token tail spike due to kernel/batcher interplay causing SM slice tilt and VRAM churn". linked PRs and dashboards in the issue.

Maria G: thanks all. if we see reoccurrence after batcher change we escalate to deeper kernel runtime profiling. :thumbsup:

Joel B: reaction :thumbsup:

rahul: reaction :rocket:

SRE Sam: reaction :white_check_mark:
